v.rationale:
All three implementations are nearly identical in their core logic. Each adds the same #[Scope] inactiveFor with a grouped whereNull/orWhere on '<' now()->subDays, a datetime cast, a nullable timestamp migration, an attribute-based command validated with filter_var, and Schedule::command()->dailyAt('06:00')->appendOutputTo(). None of them adds onOneServer, which is correct for a single server. All test suites pass. I probed each one with these --days values: 0, '', ' 7', '+7', '007', very large numbers, and a future login. Behaviour matched across all three, except that impl-2 rejects 0 while impl-1 and impl-3 accept it. Neither choice is wrong. I found no functional bugs in the counting logic.

The ranking comes down to test quality and small choices. impl-2 has the most thorough tests: exact output, a deterministic boundary via travelTo(startOfSecond), and checks on the schedule's timezone and output path. Against that, it hardcodes an unrequested Europe/Copenhagen timezone on a UTC app, leaves a duplicate commented line in Pest.php, and prints '1 users'. impl-1 has the leanest and most modern code ($this->fail(), no extra factory state), but its loose ': 1' substring assertions weaken its tests. impl-3 is clean, but its schedule test does not check the log output, it includes a low-value schema test, and it freezes time inconsistently. Overall: impl-2 > impl-1 > impl-3, with small margins between them.
